key_insight: Interferometric reconstruction shows that nonlinear four-wave-mixing light from (PEA)2PbI4 can be evaluated as a quantum-communication resource, with coherence-time sampling lowering the Holevo bound and revealing more indistinguishable polarization states.
engineering_relevance: The results suggest 2D perovskite nonlinear emitters could be engineered as tunable, material-based photon sources for secure optical links, with population-time control offering the strongest throughput gains.
method: Polarization-resolved interferometric field measurements of four-wave-mixing signals
Microscopic nonlinear Bloch-vector response model to reconstruct effective single-photon polarization density matrices
Compute Holevo bound and effective secret-bits-per-pulse across coherence time, population time, and detection wavelength
evidence_signal: Across excitonic resonances, adding coherence time reduced the Holevo bound by about 2.6–5.8%, and population-time tuning produced higher secret-bit rates than coherence-time tuning.
watch_item: The secret-bit metric is effective and model-based rather than photon-number-resolved, so practical security and device performance still depend on measurement noise, calibration, and source stability.
paper_title: Security Metrics for Nonlinear Optical Light Sources from Interferometric Field Reconstruction
